sections.content: Postpositions in Hungarian follow an unmarked nominative noun: *a Duna mentén* ("along the Danube"), *a folyó mellett* ("beside the river"), *a két part között* ("between the two banks"). In B1 geographical descriptions, postpositions are often compounded with participial modifiers (*-ó/-ő*) to create dense, informative landscape descriptions: *a folyó mentén húzódó dombok* ("the hills stretching along the river").

sections.title: Key spatial postpositions for geography
rows: beside X, next to X (settlements, borders)
between X and Y (geographical boundaries, rivers)
beyond X / on this side of X (as seen in *Dunántúl*)
on the bank / shore of X

items.spanish: Budapest a Duna két partján, hegyek és síkságok között egyesült.
items.english: Budapest united on the two banks of the Danube, between hills and plains.

items.spanish: A Tisza mentén fekvő alföldi városok híresek mezőgazdaságukról.
items.english: The lowland cities lying along the Tisza are famous for their agriculture.

items.spanish: A Dunántúl a Duna jobb partján túl elterülő dombos táj.
items.english: Transdanubia is the hilly landscape extending beyond the right bank of the Danube.

items.spanish: A Balaton északi partja mentén vulkanikus tanúhegyek magasodnak.
items.english: Along the northern shore of Lake Balaton, volcanic buttes rise up.

sections.content: Notice how the historical name *Dunántúl* is formed from *Dunán túl* ("beyond the Danube"). When describing Hungarian regions, using *mentén* for watercourses and *között* for regional relations creates elegant, authentic phrasing.
